deepdive.netdebt: ** Interest-bearing debt reduced INR 27 cr in FY26

profile.mgmt: Sanjay Thakker (Promoter, Chairman & ED); Aryaman Thakker (ED); Surendra Agarwal (CFO). Hosted/moderated by ICICI Securities (Ronak Mehta)
profile.subseg: New vehicles by brand; after-sales/service (incl. accident/insurance repair); spares/parts; pre-owned; EV (BYD/MG/Mahindra)
profile.themes: EV penetration / new-energy vehicles (BYD/MG/Mahindra ramp); GST 2.0 + cess rationalization; OEM India-localization (Jeep-Tata, Honda 10-launch revamp, Mercedes 40-product global cycle)

bull_bear.body: - Interest-bearing debt down INR 27 cr in FY26; FY27 debt expected to fall further on strong OCF (INR 267.5 cr; OCF/EBITDA 0.95) — unless expansion requires fresh long-term debt. Dividend tripled to INR 1.5/sh (from INR 0.50). Priority on cash generation.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **OEM dependence / concentration:** Standalone profit heavily Mercedes-linked; quotas (BYD CBU 2,500-unit cap), OEM supply challenges, OEM price/strategy decisions all flow through. No OEM margin renegotiation so far, but mgmt "wait and watch."
- Macro/geopolitical ("war"), FOREX (drives OEM price hikes + spare costs), CV demand hesitancy.
- **GST/cess overhang:** Cess matter pending before Supreme Court (no cess on vehicles currently); had to liquidate cess-laden stock earlier (margin pressure noted in H1).
- After-sales 20% margin may not persist (10-yr avg ~18%).
- EV transition modestly dilutive to long-run service revenue (~12–14% per global study).
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident but disciplined — repeatedly urges judging the business annually, not quarterly. "Year of consolidation / reap benefits / get profits back." Cost focus emphasized strongly. Candid on VW exit, BYD quota issue, one-time nature of inventory gain, and Indian growth story "intact and kicking."
bull_bear.title: Management tone

bull_bear.body:
- ~47% of service income is insurance-funded accident repair → structurally protected and EV-resilient (battery replacement more expensive than ICE repair).
- ASP "price-hike benefit" is explicitly a one-time gain on held stock, not a recurring margin lift — important for modeling.
- Standalone (Mercedes-heavy) PAT recovered INR 7 cr → INR 12 cr; quarter bonuses (sales & after-sales) cause lumpy quarterly comparisons.
- A "promoter" reclassifying to non-promoter category holds zero shares (family separation) — no real overhang.
- Mercedes measured by per-car realization (ASP up, units flat/down on VAHAN) with VAHAN lag in some states (Telangana etc.) — VAHAN can understate.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Outlet expansion is funded through internal accruals rather than external capital, per the strategic network expansion slide.
- Net Cash Flows from Operating Activities to EBITDA conversion improved from 0.41 (FY22) to 0.28, 0.18, 0.65 and 0.95 (FY26), with operating cash flows of Rs. 764 / 710 / 408 / 1,520 / 2,675 Mn against EBITDA of Rs. 1,873 / 2,500 / 2,272 / 2,349 / 2,830 Mn over FY22–FY26.
- EBITDA margin on proforma revenue over the expansion phase: 6.3% (FY22), 7.4%, 6.9%, 5.8%, 5.8% (FY26) — i.e. margin absorbed the cost of network build-out rather than expansion being deferred.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Mercedes-Benz:** ASP raised to INR 73 lakh (Q4) from INR 69 lakh (Q3); top-end vehicles ~20% of MB sales. New V-Class & electric CLA launched (deliveries from current qtr); new S-Class in June = brand's first plug-in hybrid in India. Global 40-product cycle over next few years; India onslaught from "next year." Standalone (largely Mercedes) PAT jumped to INR 12 cr from INR 7 cr.
- **BYD:** Car supplies arriving from April; 3 models homologated (Sealion 7, Atto 3, eMAX) — currently **CBU route** (hoping for CKD over time); homologation removes the 2,500-unit cap. Hybrids expected later this year. Pune sales+service ops July → market-share gain.
- **Honda:** India "strong comeback" with 10 upcoming launches revamping entire line-up; new City launched, ZR-V Hybrid SUV & Alpha Electric SUV announced. Landmark = Honda's largest partner in India.
- **Jeep (Stellantis):** New Jeep SUV in collaboration with Tata Motors, developed in India + exported; India becoming a key dev/production hub.
- **JSW MG Motors:** MG Windsor = highest-selling EV model in India; 3 new models (EV/hybrid/ICE) this year — Majestor delivery starts this month; MG Select (premium) positive first year, one more model planned.
- **Mahindra & Mahindra:** Strong momentum; outlets stabilized; new Hyderabad after-sales facility (July) on strong service demand.
- **Volkswagen:** Exited one unprofitable VW outlet (the press "stopped stores" rumor); remains VW's only dealer in Gujarat (profitable locations retained); will size outlet count to demand, mindful of written-down value.
- **Kia:** New-gen Seltos strengthening demand; Hyderabad workshop (operational March) ramping; more products this year.
business.title: Segment detail (by brand)

business.body:
- ✅ EV penetration rising → BYD/MG/Mahindra portfolio + insurance-funded accident-repair after-sales largely insulates Landmark's service annuity.
- ⭐ OEM India-localization wave (Jeep-Tata, Honda 10 launches, Renault multi-launch, Mercedes 40-product cycle) → Landmark as multi-brand, largest-partner dealer is a direct beneficiary of the product onslaught.

---
business.title: Challenges → Beneficiaries ✅/⭐

business.body:
- Described as the "1st multi-brand, multi-location Indian Auto Retailer" and a "Professionally managed Premium & Luxury Auto Retailer" with "27+ Years of Leadership".
- "Strong Portfolio of Brands: Well positioned to cater to evolving mobility needs across ICE, Hybrid & EV segments" — Mercedes-Benz, BYD, MG, Mahindra, Honda, Kia, Renault, Volkswagen, Jeep & Citroën and Ashok Leyland.
- The brand slide carries four "#1 Partner" tags alongside the brand line-up, indicating Landmark is the largest dealer partner for four of its OEMs (the extraction does not preserve which four).
- Customer base of 5,50,000+ built over the network; management frames the after-sales arm as "High Growth, High Margin, High EBIDTA, High ROCE & Non-cyclical".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [New revenue stream] Business arrangement with ChargeZone®, described as "Industry's first Business Arrangement between a retailer and a service provider": ChargeZone gives Landmark EV customers wallet credit usable at its locations, Landmark promotes ChargeZone to onboard new and existing customers, and "for each onboarded customer ChargeZone will pay Landmark a percentage share of the Charging Revenue", securing "an additional source of recurring revenue".
- [ChargeZone scale] Counterparty profile as given: 16,000+ charge points, 1,500+ live chargers, 600+ public charging stations, 110 MW+ installed capacity, 26+ states/UT, 490K+ app users, 50K+ kms highways electrified, 15,000+ public EVs served daily, 9+ Mn energy units sold per month, 20+ EV fleet & eMSP partners, 5X growth in past 3 years.
- [Revenue definition] "Proforma Revenue = Reported Revenue + Value of Cars sold under Mercedes-Benz Agency Model less Agency Commission" — proforma and reported revenue are materially different bases (Q1FY27: Rs. 17,325 Mn proforma vs Rs. 13,024 Mn reported) and must not be interchanged.
- [Industry/regulatory] "The auto industry continues its strong growth trajectory after GST 2.0 reforms. Having set up meaningful capacity in the previous years, the company is able to participate in this growth very well."
- [Structure] Landmark Cars Limited operates through thirteen 100%-owned subsidiaries including Landmark Cars (East), Landmark Automobiles, Automark Motors, Landmark Commercial Vehicles, Landmark Mobility, Landmark Premium Cars, Benchmark Motors, Watermark Cars, Motorone India (automobile products & accessories), Landmark Lifestyle Cars (Citroën), Landmark Luxury Retail (retail trading of luxury items) and Aeromark Cars.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: - EBITDA growth (+30%) outpaced revenue (+17%) on cost optimization; employee + other opex held at internal benchmark ~4% of proforma revenue; reductions in manpower & other costs %. Cost discipline described as "in our DNA." Margin uplift on price hikes is marginal (margin on higher base), not material; the real gain is the one-time held-inventory differential.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Highest-ever annual turnover/GP/EBITDA (EBITDA INR 283 cr, margin 5.8%); after-sales crossed INR 1,000 cr; Q4 EBITDA INR 79 cr (+30%, 6.2%), PAT INR 15 cr (+758%); ASP INR 23 lakh; service realization INR 30,072. Pivot from rapid expansion to consolidation; capex guided ~INR 50 cr ballpark FY27; debt down INR 27 cr; dividend tripled to INR 1.5. EV mix >21%. VW outlet exit; BYD quota normalization. Mercedes ASP INR 73 lakh (from INR 69 lakh Q3). [Prior-quarter context referenced by mgmt: after-sales margin had dipped below 18% in a recent quarter; inventory was ~30–36 days; GST/cess inventory liquidation pressured H1 FY26 margins.]
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **Capex FY27:** No large capex planned. Historic ballpark ~INR 50 cr/yr "could be taken as a ballpark" (vs elevated spend during the 18-20 month expansion). Mgmt declined to commit a hard number.
- **Expansion pace:** Deliberately slowing — "year of consolidation." Growth this year comes from already-committed projects (Pune BYD sales+service ops July; Hyderabad Mahindra after-sales facility July; "one or two other things in pipeline"), NOT fresh rapid rollout.
- **Margin:** Targeting restoration of historic profit metrics (ROCE back to double-digit as recent outlets ramp); ~6% EBITDA margin "almost reached." After-sales 20% margin — mgmt cautions against assuming the elevated print continues; 10-yr average ~18%, "will strive."
- **After-sales mix:** Continue to push ASP/realization higher (sweat assets) rather than chase service count; ~47% of service income is accident/insurance repair.
- **New brands/outlets:** No new brand additions flagged; opportunity to acquire dealerships remains large (global top dealers do 2–2.5% of national auto sales; Landmark "not even halfway there").
- **Demand:** April & May volume growth healthy; OEM price hikes in April with another expected June → supports ASP. EV penetration expected to rise materially with current fuel prices.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — explicit)

outlook.body:
- FY26 industry PV ~47 lakh units, +13% YoY; Landmark +20% top-line (ahead of industry). Slow H1, GST 2.0 rationalization stimulated H2 demand by lowering ownership cost.
- Demand "resilient" despite macro/"war" backdrop; only commercial vehicles showing hesitancy (last 8–10 days) + some OEM supply challenges.
- Strong waiting periods: Mercedes V-Class (~INR 1.4 cr) & electric CLA (~INR 55 lakh) waiting up to months; Kia new-gen Seltos ~2-month wait; Renault Duster (deliveries from mid-April) positive response.
- BYD: May expected to be best-ever monthly sales as supply normalizes (Q4 was supply/quota constrained).
outlook.title: Demand / Pipeline

outlook.body:
- **After-sales annuity:** Crossed INR 1,000 cr/yr; ~47% from accident/insurance-funded repair (insulated from EV transition). Spare-part price inflation (metal/FOREX) + OEM target bonuses lifting realization. Lever = ASP per service, not just count. ROCE expansion optionality as recent garages ramp.
- **EV exposure:** EVs >21% of Landmark sales vs ~5% industry PV EV penetration; BYD/MG/Mahindra positioned as the three new-energy pillars. EV after-sales impact assessed as marginal (~12–14% revenue drop per Goldman study; battery/accident repair costlier offsets lower routine service).
- **BYD ramp:** Quota normalization + Pune outlet + hybrids = major volume optionality.
- **Inventory pricing play:** Built inventory up to ~36 days (from ~30) ahead of April/June OEM price hikes → one-time held-stock gain; will revert toward ~30 days.
outlook.title: Growth / Optionality

deepdive.thesis: FY26 was the peak-investment-to-harvest inflection: after 18 months of rapid multi-brand/geography expansion, FY27 is explicitly the "year of consolidation" — sweat existing assets, restore historic profit metrics, minimal capex, with EV mix (21% of sales) and a >INR 1,000 cr after-sales annuity as the structural differentiators.
